newsitem.title: JAPAN: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - Dec 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - Dec 18.

text.p: Nomura Securities Co Ltd's group asset management affiliates, Nomura Securities Investment Trust Management Co Ltd and Nomura Investment Management Co Ltd, are to merge on October 1, 1997. The new company is expected to have combined assets of more than 15 trillion yen. The two Nomura affiliates hopes to boost their competitive edge by enhancing asset management and information gathering capabilities through the merger.

Ten leading semiconductor companies, including Fujitsu Ltd, Toshiba Corp and Matsushita Electric Industrial Co Ltd, have agreed to set up a consortium to develop a low-cost, high-performance microprocesser (MPU) by combining several chips. They aim to double current performance levels and cut prices by half.

Mitsui & Co Ltd plans to start an auction business in the United States using satellite communications from early next year, in cooperation with Japan's largest used-car auctioneer Aucnet Inc. The companies plan to sell cars, personal computers and real estate in auction through the satellite system.

Daishowa Paper Manufacturing Co Ltd is expected to post a record consolidated net profit to 14 billion yen in the business year to March 31, 1997, compared with 2.7 billion yen of red ink last year. This will be the first net profit in six years, helped by strong sales of pulp and papers in its overseas units.

Nippon Signal Co Ltd is expected to increase its current profit by 24 percent to 2.8 billion yen in the year to March 1997, while two other major railway signal makers Kyosan Electric Mfg Co Ltd and Daido Signal Co Ltd expect to mark single-digit rises in pre-tax profits.

Japan's leading three tank builders Toyo Kanetsu KK, Koyo Iron Works & Construction Co Ltd and Ishii Iron Works Co Ltd are expected to see large operation losses in the year to March 1997, hit by weak earnings in tank construction in Japan and overseas.
